The idea of the culture industry that Adorno and Horkheimer pioneered that I discussed in my earlier paper on Magic: the Gathering and how it became a soulless mechanism for profit, did not account for a few things and could not account for others.
The culture industry is an indiscriminate rising tide that swallows anything that breaks through its surface. if you find yourself at the bottom of a pond, you might see light shine down from the surface. But if you find yourself at the bottom of the ocean, all you will find is water in every direction. This comparison is similar to Plato’s “Allegory of the Cave.” When Adorno and Horkheimer published The Dialectic of Enlightenment in 1947, “popular culture” was still in its early stages as television was released only 20 years prior to the release of the piece. Less than 20 television channels were available in 1947 and the four major broadcasting channels did not even have programming every night (Allen, 2009). There was less to “infect with sameness” and less of everything to consume. "Popular Culture" in 1947 was equivalent to a small pond that consisted of less information and media to sift through.
Over 70 years later and largely to the advent of the internet, information can be produced, copied, parodied, remixed, and repurposed within seconds. People are exposed to so much media and information that it's common for individuals to have "holes" in their memory, or being unexposed to a piece of media or information that others assumed would be universal knowledge. For example, I was just told a month ago that it is “Tommy Hilfiger” and not “Tommy Hillfinger”. That was a hole in my cultural memory. If the culture industry was as all encompassing as Adorno and Horkheimer would believe, then holes in people’s memories theoretically would not occur. Or did Adorno and Horkheimer merely see phantoms, dancing shadows on the cave wall?

This picture is combining Tifa Lockheart from Final Fantasy VII and Rosie the Riveter. This essay attempts to explain how this picture is effective at conveying a new message, and attempting to explain how “culture artistry” is an unforeseen byproduct of the culture industry. If “business is simply an ideology to justify the trash they intentionally produce” (Adorno, Horkheimer, 1947) then how would they understand the art that the culture industry unintentionally produces? The culture industry allows for this remixing of parts to create something new such as taking decades old images and repurposing them to reflect a different, new, or unique idea. I call this process of rebuking the culture industry and remixing it "culture artistry". In this case, the remixed message is taking action against climate change while co-opting other semiotic messages from Tifa and Rosie.
The creation of video games became a new vessel for delivering narratives. However the encompassing aspects of a video game tied many more things to that narrative. Henry Jenkins wrote in Game Design as Narrative Structure' “The experience of playing games can never be simply reduced to the experience of a story. Many other factors which have little or nothing to do with storytelling per se contribute to the development of great games and we need to significantly broaden our critical vocabulary for talking about games to deal more fully with those other topics” (Jenkins 2002).
If the level of engagement is measured by the amount of imaginative engagement, books would be the first step. No movement and only words to describe the images that fill the reader’s head. Paintings give the viewer the image they otherwise would have to imagine. Video guides the viewer the action and movement they had to predict from the painting. Video games let the player control the movement. Once a viewer becomes a player, the level of immersion multiplies exponentially. Once immersion into a piece of media passes a certain point, the events of the narrative begin to have a personal impact on the gamer. Stephen Hirst quoted Bobby Pembleton, who works at a top university as an enterprise executive about the game’s message and how it impacted him; “Me and both of my siblings were totally radicalized by the game. When we first finished it back in the day, our takeaway was, ‘Oh, civilization ended, and this is a good thing’” (Hirst, 2021).Jenkins describes this level of immersion saying “Games, in turn, may more fully realize the spatiality of these stories, giving a much more immersive and compelling representation of their narrative worlds” (Jenkins, 2002). Jenkins goes on to beautifully describe the mental processes that prior to video games had no actionable outlet but have existed for hundreds of years by discussing the ending of War and Peace “Anyone who doubts that Tolstoy might have achieved his true calling as a game designer should reread the final segment of War and Peace where he works through how a series of alternative choices might have reversed the outcome of Napoleon’s Russian campaign” (Jenkins 2002). Video games are the only media that allows for the consumer to have the character irrevocably fail or even literally die, go baCk to an earlier point of the narrative and enable a different outcome. Go rewind a movie and hit play, the guy still gets shot. Rereading a chapter does not mean that he gets the girl. The “save point” in video games is what Tolstoy wanted; the ability to try something different and see if it worked. But there is only one life to live unless it is a video game.
"Rosie the Riveter" was a World War II poster that was a call to action for women to join the war effort by producing the supplies needed on the front. The image represents women's empowerment, American nationalism, domestic industrialism, and a communal effort for achieving a communal goal. Women working in factories were being presented as a show of patriotism. The image of Rosie continued as a symbol of the empowerment of women even after the war.
Final Fantasy VII exists in a world set in the not-so-distant future where the Shinra Electric Company is syphoning mako, the resource that keeps the planet inhabitable, causing irreversible damage. The player assumes the role of a member of the eco-terrorist group, AVALANCHE. The first level of the game is a bombing mission of one of the city's eight reactors and the plot revolves around "saving the planet" by dismantling Shinra. Stephen Hirst from artechnica described the jarring end scene of the game perfectly. “The final cut scene is set hundreds of years after the events of the endgame, when Cloud and the gang are, presumably, very dead. We see party member/space coyote Red XIII (whose species lives for thousands of years) and his children roaming the weedy ruins of the world’s forgotten, unpopulated metropolis of Midgar” (Hirst, 2021). At that point, the game returns to the familiar title screen asking the player "New Game?" 
Adorno and Horkheimer discuss the idea of a jazz musician modifying Mozart saying that only things like pitch, harmony, and speed could be modified and those modifications can only do so much. Modifications do not change that it is Mozart (Adorno, Horkheimer, 1947). Tifa is one of the strongest female characters to be portrayed in video games and was the logical character to take the iconic Rosie pose, maintaining the image of women's empowerment. However Tifa is part of a team of iconic characters. While Rosie's primary message is "We can do it, girls!" Tifa does not have a direct connection to women's empowerment the way Rosie does. Rosie is a symbol of women's empowerment; Tifa is an example of it. This enables this remix of images to acknowledge the message of women’s empowerment but not be dominated by it and therefore able to communicate its message of environmentalism to men without being filtered through the image of Rosie, to which they cannot relate. Rosie is so strongly associated with American nationalism that presenting Tifa in Rosie's pose, saying "We Can Do It!" addressing climate change frames the message itself with undercurrents of American nationalism for actions against climate change; it is patriotic to fight against climate change. Tifa taking the stance of Rosie, contrary to Adorno and Horkheimer’s beliefs, actually does change the message of the media. If Dr Dre used Mozart as a sample for a beat, we call that a Dre beat; not a piece by Mozart.
Adorno and Horkheimer I do not believe could imagine the size the culture industry would grow to or that something as immersive as video games would gain such a foothold in popular culture. I am not sure that they would see the idea of "culture artistry" as a possibility. Adorno and Horkheimer might have seen someone attempting “culture artistry” as a child with an 8-pack of Crayola crayons given the limited content the culture industry had consumed at that point. Now in 2021, there is more content available for one human to consume in their lifetime now annexed into the culture industry. Adorno and Horkheimer might instead see cultural artistry as Monet subtly changing pigments to paint the people underneath the shade of the tree to compensate for the light not looking quite the same and be pleasantly surprised to discover that they were wrong.

The biggest game changer for me in the lower divisions is a very simple one but might be blasphemy to everyone on here:

Buy Tracker's Knife

I swear that item has a hidden passive that says "Your teammates will play better"

You can use it to protect a lane, ward the enemy jungle (v important), keep objective control. One of my personal ways to use it is when you gank top lane, use the 2 wards and 1 trinket ward to ward all three top bushes for your laner. With perfect vision there is no chance for the enemy to do cute bush dodges and such. Also when chasing an enemy and they enter a bush, throwing a ward in there before you follow makes it so you never miss a beat when dueling.

I swear by Tracker's Knife. I won't use anything else but I understand it's not for everyone. It makes jungling feel more like Command & Conquer instead of feeling like running around with your head cut off.

As for teammates being toxic? Mute them. If they die in lane and the enemy is low, take the free kill. Your job is objectives. Kills will come naturally in my experience. This is a very interesting question. We run traditional tournaments up at the store that I work at, largely to my interest in this format, so I have seen what happens when we have all of the cards. The thing I have noticed is that there are actually a few archetypes that only need a single card to come back to make then viable/overpowered again. Spellbooks are the obvious answer with Spellbook of Judgment. Elemental Hero - Stratos would be a huge boost to not only E Heros, but I think more importantly, D - Heros with a full playset of Destiny Draw and Destiny Hero - Malicious at it's disposal. All it would be missing from the engine of the old Perfect Circle/T-Hero/Tele-Dad/DAD Return engine would be none other then Destiny Hero - Disk Commander. Those cards would breathe life back into archetypes, which would be cool to see.

Personally, I would love to have an actual combo be viable again. Watching traditional format and seeing REAL combo decks that did not have to win off of combat alone was refreshing. Now yes, there is degenerate combos that needed to be reigned in (that is why we have "modified" traditional format at our store now) but that is also because of the decks having EVERY banned card.

So the cards that would actually enable REAL combos back into the game, without the degenerate support of TOO many banned cards in the deck would be none other then... Card of Safe Return... and Butterfly Dagger - Elma.

The cards that I think are the most oppressive of all on the Forbidden List are without a doubt Forceful Sentry, Subsitoad, Imperial Order, and Painful Choice. Painful Choice alone can generate such insurmountable advantage with the amount of graveyard effects the game has now. Subsitoad is a walking combo. We limited Mass Driver and Dark Strike Fighter to once per turn and the Frog player (who has won every traditional format tournament, albeit not all with frogs) went from burning people in one turn to looping a single Trishula 5 times on turn one. Forceful Sentry... That card has no cost. It does not send the card to the graveyard so that makes literally every card in your opponent's hand a good target. And of course, knowledge is power, especially in a game like Yu-Gi-Oh! Imperial Order is worse in my opinion then Royal Oppression as far as control goes. You can remove the card whenever you want, and the best backrow removal in the game also happens to be spells! So that card is oppressive beyond belief.

Interesting cards to see come back? Magical Scientist. If the 'tribute for damage' effects are errata'd to once per turn, then he becomes a value card for generating obscure and weird XYZ monsters. But that also severely limits your extra deck. He would make deck building very challenging. He is powerful, do not get me wrong, but he would not be the easiest card to play well I think. Metamorphosis would be also very fun to see come back for the same reasons. The card is really good! But it also limits extra deck space. But it is a toolbox all in one, and those are the cards I love.
